summary: The first C-owned output mismatch remains pray.c:eval_offering at step 124, but the source defect is the altar-mask alias read by dosacrifice. The recording identifies the destination as Arc-loca and the selected altar as the upper lawful altar. C creates Arc-loca altars through sp_lev.c:create_altar, which writes levl[x][y].altarmask; rm.h defines altarmask as an alias of flags. The JavaScript special-level create_altar writes loc.flags, but pray.js:a_align reads only loc.altarmask. With no alias, its bitwise mask is zero and Amask2align returns A_NONE. That sends the lawful hero’s corpse offering into offer_corpse’s cross-alignment branch, consistent with the diagnostic’s unported offer_different_alignment_altar path and the stale T at the first mismatching cell.

source.branch: In dosacrifice, while standing on the upper lawful Arc-loca altar and selecting a CORPSE, altaralign is captured as a_align(u.ux,u.uy). C must read the altar alignment bits through rm.h’s altarmask/flags alias; JavaScript currently reads an absent altarmask after special-level altar creation stored those bits in flags, producing A_NONE. The downstream offer_corpse/eval_offering path then treats the lawful altar as cross-aligned.
callers: cmd.c command table (1775-1776) registers #offer to dosacrifice.
dependencies: pray.c:a_align macro (107), used by dosacrifice at 1858 to read altar alignment.
include/rm.h:214 aliases altarmask to flags; sp_lev.c:create_altar (2446-2471) stores special-level altar alignment through levl[x][y].altarmask.
dat/Arc-loca.lua:68 defines the upper altar at (26,05); sp_lev.c:lspo_altar (4283-4315) routes des.altar to create_altar.
pray.c:offer_corpse (1959-2120) consumes altaralign, then eval_offering (1898-1956) emits the first differing message for the neutral gray unicorn on the lawful altar.

evidence: The supplied C recording challenges/cases/v15/lawful-aligned-gray-unicorn-good-offering.session.json shows wizard-level teleport to the Arc-loca context at steps 18-19, then offers the gray unicorn corpse at step 123 and confirms at step 124. Its C step-124 screen is “You feel you are thoroughly on the right path.--More--”; the supplied diagnostic .cache/synthetic-scans/v15/lawful-aligned-gray-unicorn-good-offering.json records the first mismatch at that step, with C cell Y and JavaScript cell T.

The frozen level source dat/Arc-loca.lua:67-70 places three altars; line 68 is the upper altar identified by the recording’s `_comment`, with the C branch confirming the lawful alignment. It is created by des.altar -> sp_lev.c:lspo_altar (4283-4315) -> sp_lev.c:create_altar (2446-2471), which assigns the alignment mask to levl[x][y].altarmask. In include/rm.h:213-215, altarmask is a preprocessor alias for the same flags storage.

The JavaScript source path is mklev.js:create_altar (1368-1395), which stores the same mask in loc.flags. pray.js:a_align (296-299), called while dosacrifice captures altaralign at pray.c:1858, reads only state.level.at(x,y).altarmask. With no JavaScript alias, undefined & AM_MASK is zero; const.js:164-168 maps zero to A_NONE. Thus this case’s lawful altar supplies A_NONE to dosacrifice, unlike C.

The resulting A_NONE makes lawful u.ualign.type differ from altaralign. In pray.c:offer_corpse, the cross-alignment guard at 2024-2027 calls offer_different_alignment_altar instead of taking the lawful same-alignment path; this matches the supplied diagnostic’s aggregate unported entry and explains why the JavaScript screen still begins with T at step 124. The output owner is eval_offering (1920-1940), which would print the C message only after receiving the correct altaralign; the source defect is the alias read in the implemented dosacrifice/a_align path, not a missing eval_offering branch.
The separate RNG mismatch starts at step 125 in obj_resists (zap.c:1469), after the step-124 output divergence.
